summary: Sticky prefetch miss causes amplified KV reads and tail latency for consecutive continuation requests
description:
Issue summary:
BrightWrite (dedicated customer) reports sudden p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s for identical continuation requests in long-running conversational sessions. The users observe that repeat prompts (same prefix + continuation) which were previously fast now experience a ~300-700ms tail increase and sporadic request timeouts.

Impact:
- Several customer-facing chat sessions experienced degraded responsiveness for ~2 hours impacting UX for a subset of active users.
- Affects dedicated capacity in us-east only for this customer so far.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-east-dedicated-pool-3
- Gateway: api-gw-eu (fronted by CDN), requests terminate in us-east
- Model: redwood-v1-medium pinned by customer

Observed behavior:
- Identical continuation requests (same session-id, same prompt prefix) show increased p99 latency and occasional 504 from serving-runtime.
- Traces show repeated backend KV read bursts (many small get requests) on prefix keys immediately prior to generation.
- Prefetch task logs show repeated prefetch attempts for neighbouring prefix slots for the same session key.

Expected behavior:
- Repeat/continuation requests should hit local KV cache with minimal backend reads after warmup. No amplification of KV traffic for identical prefixes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a conversational session pinned to redwood-v1-medium in the customer's dedicated pool.
2) Send a repeated sequence: set of identical prompts with small continuations (streaming enabled) ~10 sequential turns.
3) Observe p95/p99 latency and check kvcache telemetry for prefix read counts and prefetch tasks.
4) Compare traces for warm/hot sessions vs affected sessions (look for repeated prefetch for same key).
logs: [2026-03-12T14:02:13Z] serving-runtime: span=gen-123 request_id=... prefetch: enqueued 7 neighbor-keys for session=brw-904
[2026-03-12T14:02:14Z] api-gateway: upstream response 504 for request_id=... latency=12000ms
investigation_notes: Support triaged — ruled out network flaps and model-side queuing (model latency stable in traces).
Tracing indicates most latency is in pre-generation step where kvcache is issuing many small reads instead of hitting in-memory shard.

Hypothesis: a prefetch/eviction race makes a hot prefix temporarily marked as stale, triggering an aggressive neighbour-key prefetch routine which amplifies backend reads and adds serialization inside the kvcache shard.

Observed a pattern where two concurrent requests for the same session cause the prefetch door to re-run due to an off-by-one timestamp check in the prefetch gate — this matches the timing of the latency spike window.
Related to recent kvcache change: prefetch batching logic deployed 2026-03-08 (PR referenced) — candidate for regression.
Reproduced in staging by running a high-concurrency repeat prompt harness; enabling 'no-prefetch' on kvcache removes the amplification and restores tail latency.
Impact limited to certain shard placements and to sessions using 'streaming + keep-alive' headers where request inter-arrival falls within the stale window.
resolution: Workaround (customer-facing): Instruct BrightWrite to temporarily pin session cache_policy to 'no-prefetch' for their critical flows. Support applied feature-flag to the customer's dedicated pool to disable prefetch for affected shard range.

Engineering fix: Rollback/patch prefetch gating logic in kvcache to correct timestamp condition and add idempotent prefetch guard. Patch: kvcache v0.24.7 -> includes guard and reduced prefetch fanout.
Rollout plan: canary 10% of us-east dedicated nodes (03/13 02:00 UTC) -> 50% (03/13 06:00 UTC) -> 100% (03/13 12:00 UTC) pending telemetry.
Postmortem follow-ups: add synthetic repeat-prompt load test to CI, add metric 'prefetch-fanout' with alerting when >5x baseline, and update runbook for disabling prefetch per-customer.
Current status: Patch deployed to canary, initial telemetry shows p99 reduced by ~420ms for canary nodes. Continuing rollouts and monitoring.
